title: Weierstrass coordinate change and completion of a henselian cylinder
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a complete Noetherian local domain, let $r\geq1$, and put $R=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Suppose $f\in\mathfrak m_R$ has nonzero reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_\Lambda R$. Write $T=t_r$. There is a continuous $\Lambda[[T]]$-algebra automorphism $c$ of $R$, of the form $c(t_i)=t_i+T^{N_i}$ for $i<r$, with $N_i>0$, and a factorization $c(f)=u g$, where $u$ is a unit of $R$, $D=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1}]]$, and $g=T^n+\sum_{i<n}b_iT^i\in D[T]$ has $n>0$ and all $b_i\in\mathfrak m_D$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Put $R_0=D[T]$, $\mathfrak q=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$, and let $H=(R_0)_{\mathfrak q}^{h}$ be the henselization [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Then $H$ is Noetherian local henselian with residue field $D/\mathfrak m_D$; the pair $(H,gH)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. The canonical map $H\to D[[T]]=R$ identifies $R$ both with the $g$-adic completion and with the maximal-ideal completion of $H$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and this map is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For $r=1$ the automorphism can be the identity.

source.place: Expose V, Theorem 1.1.1(i),(ii), Lemma 1.1.3, Lemma 1.2.3, and proof 2.2.3 (the horizontal maps are completions for both topologies). For the zero-coordinate case r=1 use Theorem 1.1.1(i) without a coordinate change.

proof.text: Put $k=\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, $D=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1}]]$ and regroup coefficients to identify $R=D[[T]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] and [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base], both $D$ and $R$ are Noetherian complete local rings, with maximal ideals $(\mathfrak m_\Lambda,t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1})$ and $(\mathfrak m_\Lambda,t_1,\ldots,t_{r-1},T)$ respectively. The regrouping sends the coefficient at $(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ to the coefficient of $t_1^{e_1}\cdots t_{r-1}^{e_{r-1}}$ in the coefficient of $T^{e_r}$; finite convolution gives multiplicativity. These statements include $r=1$, when $D=\Lambda$.

source.place: V 1.1.1, setup; the complete-local hypotheses in V 1.1.3.

proof.text: The coefficientwise reduction of $f$ is nonzero: since $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ is finitely generated, a series all of whose coefficients lie in it is a sum of its finitely many generators times series, hence belongs to $\mathfrak m_\Lambda R$. In the nonzero series $\bar f\in k[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$, choose its lexicographically least supported exponent $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ by successively minimizing each coordinate. Set $w_r=1$ and, downwards, $w_i=1+\sum_{j>i}a_jw_j$. If $b\ne a$ is supported and $i$ is its first differing coordinate, then $b_i>a_i$ and $w\cdot b-w\cdot a\geq w_i-\sum_{j>i}a_jw_j>0$. Thus $a$ is the unique exponent of least weight. Substitute $t_i\mapsto t_i+T^{w_i}$ for $i<r$, fixing $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation], this and the substitution with minus signs define continuous maps for the maximal-ideal topology: all substituted variables lie in the maximal ideal, and truncations of total degree $<N$ compute the maps modulo its $N$th power. Their composites fix every variable and constant, hence every truncation, hence every series by separatedness. They are inverse automorphisms and fix $\Lambda[[T]]$. After putting $t_1=\cdots=t_{r-1}=0$ and reducing modulo $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, the substituted series is $\sum_b\bar f_bT^{w\cdot b}$; each coefficient is a finite sum since all weights are positive. Its least coefficient is $\bar f_a\ne0$. For $r=1$ the same argument uses the identity substitution.

source.place: V 1.1.1(ii); explicit least-weight argument for the stated triangular coordinate change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-weierstrass-preparation-complete-local] over the complete local ring $D$ to $c(f)\in D[[T]]$. The last conclusion of Step 2 is exactly its nonzero-reduction hypothesis. This yields $c(f)=ug$ with $u$ a unit and $g=T^n+\sum_{i<n}b_iT^i$, $b_i\in\mathfrak m_D$. The substitutions preserve the maximal ideal, so $c(f)$ is a nonunit. If $n=0$, monicity gives $g=1$, a contradiction. Therefore $n>0$ and $g\in(\mathfrak m_D,T)$.

source.place: V 1.1.1(i); positivity of the order follows from f in the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Put $R_0=D[T]$, $\mathfrak q=(\mathfrak m_D,T)$ and $A=(R_0)_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $A$ is Noetherian; its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak qA$ and its residue field is $k$. Apply [lem-per-local-pair-henselization-comparison] to identify the specified ordinary henselization $H=A^h$ with the henselization of $(A,\mathfrak qA)$. Hence $H$ is local henselian with $\mathfrak m_H=\mathfrak qH$ and residue field $k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-noetherian-completion] to this Noetherian pair: $H$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], $R$ is henselian. The inclusion $R_0\to R$ extends to a local map $A\to R$, since a polynomial outside $\mathfrak q$ has unit constant coefficient in $D$ and therefore is a unit in $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring]. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] now gives the canonical local map $H\to R$.

For every $N\geq1$, truncation in $T$ gives $R_0/\mathfrak q^N\xrightarrow{\sim}R/(\mathfrak m_DR+(T))^N$. Surjectivity follows since the tail starting at $T^N$ vanishes. For injectivity, [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] says a series lies in the target ideal exactly when its coefficient of $T^j$ lies in $\mathfrak m_D^{N-j}$ for $j<N$; for polynomials this is exactly membership in $\mathfrak q^N$, by expanding $(\mathfrak m_D,T)^N$. Every $s\notin\mathfrak q$ is already invertible in this quotient: write $s=a(1+v)$ with $a\in D^\times$, $v\in\mathfrak q$, and invert $1+v$ by $\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-v)^j$. Thus localization induces $A/(\mathfrak qA)^N\cong R_0/\mathfrak q^N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-flat-quotients], $A/(\mathfrak qA)^N\xrightarrow{\sim}H/\mathfrak m_H^N$. These are all the maps induced by $R_0\to H\to R$, so commute with reduction in $N$. Taking inverse limits and using the maximal-ideal completeness of $R$ proves that the canonical map $H\to R$ identifies $R$ with $\widehat H_{\mathfrak m_H}$.

source.place: V 2.2.3, maximal-ideal completion assertion; explicit truncation comparison, Stacks 0AGU.

proof.text: The ring $H$ is Noetherian local by Step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] makes its maximal-ideal completion map faithfully flat. The identification of Step 5 is induced by $H\to R$, so this is precisely the required faithful flatness of that canonical map.

source.place: V 1.1.3, faithful flatness used in its proof; Stacks Tag 00MC.

proof.text: To check $(H,gH)$ directly in the idempotent definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], take any finite $H$-algebra $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product], write $B=\prod_jB_j$ with local structural maps $H\to B_j$. Since $g\in\mathfrak m_H$, each $gB_j$ lies in the maximal ideal of $B_j$, and $B_j/gB_j$ is nonzero local. In a local ring an idempotent $e$ is $0$ or $1$: one of $e,1-e$ is a unit and $e(1-e)=0$. Consequently the quotient $B_j\to B_j/gB_j$ is a bijection on idempotents, sending $0,1$ to $0,1$. Taking the finite product proves the same for $B\to B/gB$, including the zero-algebra case (empty product). This proves the asserted henselian pair without changing from maximal-ideal henselianity to a smaller ideal without argument.

source.place: V Lemma 1.2.3; elementary idempotent proof using Stacks 04GH.

proof.text: Fix $N\geq1$. Modulo $\mathfrak m_D$, the polynomial $g^N$ is $T^{nN}$; it is monic, so is again distinguished. Apply [lem-per-distinguished-polynomial-quotient] to obtain the canonical isomorphism $C_N:=D[T]/(g^N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R/(g^NR)$. The latter is nonzero local since $g\in\mathfrak m_R$, and it is henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-henselian-pair], because $R$ is henselian by Step 4. The preimage in $D[T]$ of its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak q$, as is seen by composing with $R\to k$ (constant term followed by residue). Thus all elements outside $\mathfrak q$ are units in $C_N$, and localization gives a canonical isomorphism $A/g^NA\xrightarrow{\sim}C_N$. In particular $A/g^NA$ is itself henselian local.

source.place: V Lemma 1.1.3, comparison modulo Q=P^N; V 1.1.1(i).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-henselization-quotient-at-prime], $H/g^NH$ is the ordinary henselization of $A/g^NA$. But the latter ring is already henselian by Step 8. Its henselization structure map is an isomorphism: [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] applied to the identity supplies a retraction, and uniqueness applied to maps back to the henselization makes the other composite the identity. Therefore $A/g^NA\to H/g^NH$ is an isomorphism. The local map $H/g^NH\to R/g^NR$ induced by the canonical map agrees on $A/g^NA$ with the isomorphism of Step 8, hence is also an isomorphism. These are canonical quotient maps, and their squares with the quotient projections for $N+1\to N$ commute on every element of $H$.

source.place: V Lemma 1.1.3, passage to all powers; Stacks Tag 05WQ (lemma-quotient-henselization).

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-complete-local-subideal], the complete Noetherian local ring $R$ is complete also for the ideal $gR\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$. Hence taking inverse limits in Step 9 gives $\widehat H_{gH}=\varprojlim_NH/g^NH\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_NR/g^NR=R$. The map from $H$ is the original canonical map because its $N$th coordinate is reduction of that map modulo $g^N$. Together with Steps 3--7 this proves all the clauses, and the construction in Step 2 was the identity for $r=1$.

source.place: V Lemma 1.1.3, final inverse-limit argument, and V 2.2.3, both completion topologies.
